About the Chatham Rise fishing area

The area is within the South-East fishing area but has different rules. It covers the waters of the Chatham Rise, including the Chatham Islands, out to the exclusive economic zone.

All recreational fishing is covered by the rules. This includes potting, netting, and all other fishing methods.

The rules: size and catch limits, closed areas, and special restrictions

Catch or bag limits

Finfish includes all species of finfish of the classes Agnatha, Chondrichthyes, and Osteichthyes, at any stage of their life history, whether living or dead.

The accumulation/possession of finfish beyond one day’s daily limit entitlement is prohibited.

There is a combined daily bag limit of 30 finfish per fisher (excluding specified baitfish and freshwater eels). This means that you can have a combination of up to 30 of any finfish in total. For example, you could have 10 flatfish, 15 spiny dogfish, and 5 red cod. As long as you have no more than 30 in total.

There are also species with individual daily limits within the combined daily bag limit of 30 (Table 1). You must not exceed individual species limits. For example, there is a daily limit of 5 blue cod. This means you could have 5 blue cod, 5 kahawai, 10 flatfish, and 10 spiny dogfish.

Any catch taken from the area is included in the combined daily bag limit for the South-East fishing area

In addition to the combined daily bag limit of 30, you can take a maximum of 50 of any combination of baitfish species (Table 2) and a maximum of 2 freshwater eels (Table 3). For example, you could take 10 flatfish, 15 spiny dogfish, 5 red cod, and 50 baitfish.

Remember, there may be other specific rules in some areas. For example, a harbour might have different size limits for certain species. Check the 'special restrictions' section on this page for more information.

Blue cod

Rule

Pot construction

Rigid square mesh, where:

  • the squares in the mesh must be at least 54mm by 54mm
  • the mesh should be strong, and not easily bent or reshaped.

Accumulation Limit

The accumulation/possession of finfish beyond one day’s daily limit entitlement is prohibited.

Measurable state

All blue cod must be landed in a measurable state. The following measurable states apply:

  • Chatham Islands blue cod management area – whole or gutted, and/or headed**.

**Where permitted, blue cod headed state minimum length is 24cm and is measured from the base of the side pectoral fin to the middle ray of the tail fin.

Eating blue cod on the boat

Fishers may possess blue cod in another state if it is immediately eaten on board the fishing vessel from which it was taken. Any fish eaten form part of the daily limit.

The accumulation/possession of shellfish beyond one day’s daily limit entitlement is prohibited.

Shellfish are considered "taken" (collected or harvested) when they cannot freely return to the water. For example, when you put them in a bag. When you're gathering/collection, you can never possess more than your daily limit.

All shellfish to which a minimum size restriction applies (including pāua, scallops and dredge oysters) must be landed in the shell and cannot be shucked or shelled seaward of the mean high-water mark. This includes transporting on the water.

Dredge oysters and scallops may be opened for immediate consumption onboard the vessel. Any scallops and dredge oysters eaten form part of your daily limit. Any scallops and dredge oysters not eaten must be landed in the shell.

Underwater breathing apparatus (UBA): No person may take pāua using UBA or be in possession of pāua while in possession of UBA. This includes possession in or on any vessel or vehicle.

This section has the rules for both:

  • spiny rock lobster
  • packhorse lobster.

The accumulation/possession of rock lobster beyond one day’s daily limit entitlement is prohibited.

Remember, there may be other specific rules in some areas. Check the 'special restrictions' section on this page for more information.

Daily bag limits

Maximum of 2 rock lobster (both species combined) on any one day.

Learn how to measure rock lobster and identify the sex:

Rock lobster (crayfish): rules and guidelines

Other rules and protections

There are rules for gathering rock lobster/crayfish that cover:

  • protected types
  • banned gathering methods
  • pot construction and use.
Protected types

Some types of rock lobster are protected. You must return them to the water straight away. Protected rock lobsters are:

  • undersized rock lobster
  • any female rock lobster carrying external eggs ("in berry") – these are carried on the underside of the tail
  • any rock lobster in the soft shell stage
  • any rock lobster that cannot be measured (for example, because of damage to the tail preventing accurate measurement). Specific exemptions for very large rock lobster with damaged tails mean you can keep:
    • Spiny rock lobsters that weigh 600g or more, or have a carapace (body) length of 110mm or more.
    • Packhorse rock lobsters that weigh 2kg or more, or have a tail length of 216mm or more.
Banned gathering methods
  • You cannot possess rock lobster seaward of the high watermark in an unmeasurable state.
  • No spring-loaded loops or lassos – hand operated only.
  • No spears or puncturing devices – it is an offence to possess a speared rock lobster.
  • Do not remove external eggs from any rock lobster.
  • No baited nets.
  • Maximum of 3 rock lobster pots per fisher.
  • Maximum of 6 rock lobster pots from a vessel for 2 or more fishers.

Closed Season

There is a closed season for rock lobster in quota management area CRA6, which includes the Chatham Islands. The closed season is in place from 1 March to 30 April every year. During the closed season, you cannot:

  • take any rock lobster from quota management area CRA6.
  • fish using any rock lobster pot from quota management area CRA6.
  • possess any rock lobster taken from quota management area CRA6.

Accumulation refers to the aggregation and possession of daily fish catch in excess of more than one day’s legal possession entitlement for any person, which is unlawful in the Chatham Rise area.

Food safety warnings

We issue warnings when shellfish are unsafe to eat because of contamination with biotoxins.

Check for warnings

Report poaching

You can report poaching, suspicious, or illegal activity online:

Report illegal fishing (such as poaching)

You can also:

  • call 0800 4 POACHER (0800 47 62 24), or
  • email poacher@mpi.govt.nz

You can help us investigate by providing:

  • the location
  • vehicle/trailer registration number
  • boat name
  • description of the person.

When reporting any suspected poaching put your personal safety first. All calls and personal details are treated as confidential.

It is illegal to buy, sell or swap recreationally caught seafood

These are offences against the Fisheries Act which can result in fines up to $250,000.
